commands.description: Turns the cues of a caption track into graphic clips, one per cue at the cue's time, so the text can be animated, restyled and moved like a title (Essential Graphics, graphic.applyPreset, Effect Controls). Each is a text layer in the track's caption style - font, size, colours, outline, shadow, background box, alignment, placement, line spacing - as paragraph text in a box as wide as the caption block and as tall as its lines: the box grows with the text, and a caption at the bottom (top) is pinned to the frame's edge, so editing it to a longer text grows it upwards (downwards) from the safe margin. Lower and upper case are applied; the kinetic animation looks, speaker names, punctuation and accent rules are not (they belong to caption rendering). The graphics go on new video tracks on top (more than one when cues overlap), or on "track" when it is free under every cue. "captions" says what happens to the cues: "hide" switches the caption track off so the text is not drawn twice (default), "keep" leaves it showing, "remove" deletes the track. One undo step.

The raw motion is cached per media, so redoing an effect whose footage was analysed before is quick. Effects that cannot be analysed (a nested clip's own, a freeze frame, a switched-off effect) are listed under `skipped`. Morph Cut needs no analysis step: it analyses itself as soon as it is applied. Shares the cached analysis with Warp Stabilizer's Position method. One in the clip's media's Master Clip Effects (named by `effect`) is analysed over the frames every clip of that media shows.

commands.description: Warp Stabilizer's Analyze: tracks the camera motion of a video clip's footage, smooths the camera path with the effect's settings (Result, Smoothness, Method, Preserve Scale, Framing, Maximum Scale, Action-Safe Margin, Additional Scale, Detailed Analysis, Rolling Shutter Ripple, Crop Less Smooth More) and keys the compensating transform per frame into the clip's Warp Stabilizer (added at the top of its stack when it has none), with the crop or auto-scale that hides the moving borders. The keys stay editable. Changing a setting and running it again re-smooths from the cached analysis. Method 4 (Gyro, camera metadata) takes the rotation the camera recorded in the file (GoPro HERO5 and later, Sony cameras with a gyro) instead of tracking the picture: it is synced to the picture on a few stretches of the clip (gyroSync, gyroOffset, gyroFov, gyroReadout), smoothed with the same settings and keyed as a corner pin; the result reports the camera, the sync and the field of view under `gyro`, and a file without gyro data is refused with the reason. A Warp Stabilizer in the clip's media's Master Clip Effects (named by `effect`) is analysed over the frames every clip of that media shows, so every instance plays it stabilized. Runs as a job with progress and cancel; a dry run analyses and previews the keys.

commands.description: Imports a Lottie animation (Bodymovin JSON from After Effects, LottieFiles; or a dotLottie .lottie archive) as a motion graphic: from a file ("path") or the JSON itself ("data"). With "at" it becomes a clip there; with "saveAs" a template in the project's library (both are allowed). Its texts and the colors that stay the same are template fields (named after their layers): a clip placed with "at" is an instance of the template, so Essential Graphics edits and keys them (template.setField, template.setFieldKey). Shapes, fills, strokes, gradients, trims, transforms with their easing, text, masks and precomps come in; the report lists what was approximated or dropped (images, effects, mattes, expressions, dotLottie themes and state machines...). commands.description: Imports an OGraf graphic (the EBU's open HTML graphics format) as a motion graphic template. OGraf graphics are drawn by web pages with scripts; Wabcut has no web engine and runs no scripts, so it imports a package that also ships a Lottie version of the graphic (one .json or .lottie animation in the package, or the one the manifest names in "v_wabcut_lottie"). The manifest's fields (title, name) name the template fields whose Lottie layers are called alike. "path" is the manifest (*.ograf.json: its folder is the package), a package folder or a .zip package. A package without a Lottie version fails with a message that says so (ograf.inspect lists its fields). With "at" it becomes a clip there (an instance of the template: Essential Graphics edits and keys its fields); with "saveAs" a template in the project's library.

commands.description: Premiere's Sequence > Sequence Settings on an existing sequence. duration.description: Transition length. Default 1 second. Timecode in the sequence's rate ("00:01:02:03") or ticks.

edge.description: Which edge: "head" (the clip's In point) or "tail" (its Out point).

effect.description: The transition (effect.list).

fit.description: When the media lacks frames beyond the cut: "exact" fails with how much there is, "availableHandles" shortens the transition to fit (default).

offset.description: With alignment "custom": how much of the transition lies before the cut. Timecode in the sequence's rate ("00:01:02:03") or ticks.

sequence.description: Sequence id; only needed when the project has several.

commands.title: Add Transition

commands.description: Deletes a transition; the edit point becomes a cut.
commands.name: transition.remove

sequence.description: Sequence id; only needed when the project has several.

commands.title: Remove Transition

commands.description: Changes a transition: its effect, parameters, its length on either side of the cut ("before", "after"), a new total "duration" placed by its alignment, or the alignment itself (which re-splits it; "custom" with "offset" puts the cut that far in).
commands.name: transition.set

after.description: New length after the cut. Timecode in the sequence's rate ("00:01:02:03") or ticks.

alignment.description: Where the transition sits on a cut between two clips: centered (default), starting at the cut (the outgoing clip plays on), ending at it, or custom: the cut lies "offset" into it (by default where it is now). Stored on the transition: a new duration keeps it. Ignored for a one-sided transition at a clip end with no neighbour.

before.description: New length before the cut. Timecode in the sequence's rate ("00:01:02:03") or ticks.

duration.description: New total length, split by alignment. Timecode in the sequence's rate ("00:01:02:03") or ticks.

effect.description: New transition effect.

fit.description: When the media lacks frames beyond the cut: "exact" fails with how much there is, "availableHandles" shortens the transition to fit (default).

offset.description: With alignment "custom": how much of the transition lies before the cut. Timecode in the sequence's rate ("00:01:02:03") or ticks.

sequence.description: Sequence id; only needed when the project has several.

transition.description: Transition id (sequence.summary and clip.details list them).

commands.title: Set Transition

commands.description: Whether the sequence is VR / 360 video (its projection and eye layout: sequence.setSettings "vr" sets it) and, with "media", what that item's picture is: "file" is what its spherical metadata says, "interpretation" Interpret Footage's setting (null: none), "effective" the one in use and "suits" whether the frame size fits the projection (a 360 eye is 2:1, a 180 eye 1:1).
commands.name: vr.info

media.description: A media item. A media id or exact name.

sequence.description: Sequence id; only needed when the project has several.

commands.title: VR Video Info

commands.description: Adds the VR Reorient effect to 360 / VR180 clips and sets it: "yaw" turns the sphere to the right, "pitch" up, "roll" tilts it to the right (degrees; keyframe them with clip.addKeyframe), so a different part of the scene lands straight ahead. The projection and eye layout default to the clip's (its footage's, else the sequence's); a flat clip needs "projection". One undo step.
commands.name: vr.reorient

items.description: A clip. A clip id, or {"track", "time"} for the clip there.

time.description: A time inside the clip. Timecode in the sequence's rate ("00:01:02:03") or ticks.

track.description: Track of the clip. "V1" (bottom video track), "A2", ... or a track id.

projection.description: The picture's projection. Default: the clip's.

roll.description: Degrees of tilt to the right (-3600 to 3600).

sequence.description: Sequence id; only needed when the project has several.

stereo.description: The picture's eye layout. Default: the clip's.

commands.title: VR Reorient

commands.description: The one-click podcast / interview edit, on this computer (local, free): sync the cameras and microphones (multicam by audio), lay out the episode (the multicam picture, each microphone on its own dialogue track), transcribe, Enhance Speech, loudness to -16 LUFS, remove fillers and long pauses, switch cameras to whoever speaks, captions, chapters from the topics (and YouTube chapters), optionally shorts. Without "run" it returns the plan (every step, on or off and why); with "run" it runs the enabled steps (or "steps"), as one undo step; "context" continues an earlier run.
commands.name: workflow.podcast

angles.description: Who is on which camera, for the switching (default: the analysis guesses).

angle.description: The angle: 1 = the first camera; the microphones come after the cameras.

speaker.description: Whom a close-up shows: a speaker's name ("Mic 1": the first microphone's speaker) or key.

items.description: A media item (id or name).

context.description: What earlier runs made (a previous result's "context", as it is).

sequence.description: Episode sequence id.

items.description: A media item the run transcribed.

media.description: Or all recordings: those with a picture are cameras, the rest microphones.

items.description: A media item (id or name).

mics.description: The microphone recordings (audio only). Default: the cameras' own sound.

items.description: A media item (id or name).

minChapterSeconds.description: A chapter lasts at least this long (default 60 s).

run.description: Run the steps (default false: return the plan only).

shorts.description: Also make vertical shorts of the best moments (default false).

silences.description: Shorten pauses longer than this many seconds (default 1; 0 keeps pauses).

sync.description: How the recordings are synced (default audio).

commands.title: Podcast Workflow
